newsitem.title: USA: Howard Gary & Co removed from Dade Cty, Fla., deal.
newsitem.headline: Howard Gary & Co removed from Dade Cty, Fla., deal.

text.p: Howard Gary & Co was removed from a Dade County seaport bond issue because of allegations involving company president Howard Gary, county Finance Director Ed Marquez said Wednesday.
The firm was to act as senior manager for the $30 million Port of Miami revenue bond issue, which is expected to be priced at the end of the month.

Last week, The Miami Herald reported that Gary had secretly recorded a conversation in which he offered Dade County Commissioner James Burke $100,000 to win a spot for Gary's firm on a Dade County revenue bond refunding for a recyling plant. The newspaper said Gary acted in cooperation with federal prosecutors.

Federal prosecutors have declined to comment on the allegations and neither Gary nor Burke has been charged with any wrongdoing. Burke has resigned as chairman of the county commission's finance committee but remains a commissioner.
Marquez said Gary's firm would be removed from the seaport deal at recommendation of the county manager's finance committee.

"We are taking him off the transaction, the primary reason of it being the allegations in the press," Marquez said. "We fully realize it's just allegations. There may be disclosure concerns on the issue."
He said Howard Gary & Co would remain in the county's bond underwriting pool.
"Whatever clouds there are, hopefully the allegations will be alleviated," Marquez said.
An official at Howard Gary & Co, citing company policy, declined to comment.
Marquez said the committee had recommended another firm to act as senior manager for the deal but that the firm owuld not be identified until conty officials contacted them.
The county will use proceeds from the seaport bond issue to buy a cruise ship terminal built at the Port of Miami by Carnival Corp.
